title: Open Graph/social preview metadata
learningObjectives: Explain open graph/social preview metadata and apply accurate document metadata or print structure.

understand.concept: Open Graph metadata uses meta properties such as og:title, og:description, og:type, and og:image to describe how a page may appear when shared on social platforms. Other platforms may use additional metadata such as Twitter/X card fields.
understand.whyItMatters: Social previews help people understand a link before opening it. Metadata should match the actual page, use stable absolute image URLs, and avoid misleading descriptions.
understand.analogy: A social preview is the cover card shown when a document is shared; its metadata supplies the title, summary, and image.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser metadata and search/social platform processing are governed by their respective specifications and policies.

explain.narrative: The Open Graph properties describe the title, summary, content type, and preview image for a shared page.

examples.code: <head><meta property='og:title' content='Learn HTML Forms — CodeSaathi'><meta property='og:description' content='Build accessible forms with practical HTML examples.'><meta property='og:type' content='article'><meta property='og:image' content='https://www.example.com/images/forms-preview.png'></head>
examples.explanation: The Open Graph properties describe the title, summary, content type, and preview image for a shared page.
examples.expectedOutput: A valid HTML head or print-style example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Write social preview metadata for a course lesson. Check that the title and description match the visible page and the image URL is absolute.
practise.independentTask: Prepare metadata or print styles for a sample course page. Verify paths, content accuracy, language declarations, and the print result.
hints: Use absolute URLs where metadata requires them.
Do not invent structured data claims.
Keep the visible page consistent with metadata.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Open Graph/social preview metadata</title></head><body>
<head><meta property='og:title' content='Learn HTML Forms — CodeSaathi'><meta property='og:description' content='Build accessible forms with practical HTML examples.'><meta property='og:type' content='article'><meta property='og:image' content='https://www.example.com/images/forms-preview.png'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which Open Graph property identifies the preview image?
questions.explanation: og:image provides the URL of the image used in an Open Graph preview.

questions.prompt: What is the most important rule for page metadata?
options: It must accurately describe the actual page
It should contain as many keywords as possible
It can claim features not present on the page
questions.answer: It must accurately describe the actual page
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate, consistent, and not misleading.
